name: ACC
programsInGuide: Virginia, Wake Forest, SMU, Clemson, Notre Dame, UNC, Duke, NC State, Louisville, Pitt, Stanford, Syracuse, Cal
scholarships: Up to 9.9 equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
relevance: Strongest soccer conference in the US. 13 guide schools — the most of any conference. Clemson 2× recent NCAA champions (2021, 2023), nation-leading 4 first-round picks in 2026 draft. Virginia 7× NCAA champions. SMU won 2025 ACC Tournament (first ever). UNC ACC Regular Season champs 2023. Notre Dame 27 MLS picks. Cal and Stanford add West Coast elite access.

name: Big Ten
programsInGuide: UCLA, Indiana, Maryland, Penn State, Michigan, Michigan State, Ohio State, Northwestern, Wisconsin, Rutgers, Washington
scholarships: Up to 9.9 equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
relevance: 11 guide schools — complete Big Ten coverage. Indiana #1 all-time (8 NCAA titles). UCLA #1 West Coast (4 titles). Maryland all-time MLS pipeline leader (49 picks + 7 homegrown under Cirovski). Penn State, Michigan, OSU, Wisconsin all consistently productive. Conference expansion added Washington, elevating the conference's western D1 depth.

name: Big East
programsInGuide: St. John's, Georgetown, Creighton, UConn, Providence, Villanova, Marquette, Butler, Seton Hall, DePaul, Xavier, Akron
scholarships: Up to 9.9 equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
relevance: 11 guide schools — complete Big East coverage. Georgetown (2019 champion, 42 MLS signings) and St. John's (NYC, Hospital for Special Surgery proximity) are Olivier's top fits. Creighton consistently in NCAA Tournaments. UConn, Providence, Villanova all improving. Strong northeast urban clinical networks across every school. Akron joined the Big East for men's soccer in 2023 (the MAC discontinued the sport) and won the Big East Midwest Division in 2024 and 2025 — a top-20 all-time MLS pipeline, Cleveland Clinic clinical network, coach Jared Embick contracted through 2035.

name: AAC

relevance: 10 guide schools — the most complete AAC coverage in the guide. Florida trio (FIU, USF, FAU) are Olivier's top AAC fits — warm climate, accessible GPA thresholds, strong exercise science programs. Charlotte ranked No.24 nationally in 2025.

name: Big West

scholarships: Up to 9.9 equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in

Manu Duah #1 overall 2025 MLS pick — highest Big West pick ever. UC Irvine won 2025 Big West Tournament. UC Davis won 2024 tournament. UCSD transitioning to full D1. Pac-12/Big West men's soccer partnership announced 2025 elevates the conference profile significantly.

relevance: Denver won 5 consecutive Summit League titles 2021–2025 and reached the 2024 College Cup Final Four. Moved to WCC in 2026 — a significant elevation in conference profile. HC Jamie Franks is one of the most technically precise developers in D1. Excellent city; cold winters the trade-off.

name: WAC
scholarships: Up to 9.9 equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
relevance: GCU won the 2025 WAC title and reached the NCAA Sweet 16 (beating UCLA and San Diego). Jamie Davies appointed December 2025. Phoenix — best warm major-city D1 campus outside Florida and California. Kinesiology with Banner Health clinical network.

name: Ivy League
scholarships: Zero athletic scholarships
relevance: Princeton surging — 2024+2025 Ivy Tournament doubles. No athletic scholarships — need-based financial aid only. Yale strong academically. GPA and SAT improvement essential for both programs.

name: CCCAA/NJCAA
programsInGuide: Santa Monica, Miami Dade, Iowa Western, Northeast CC, Monroe, Indian Hills, Tyler JC, Daytona State, Barton CC, Cowley CC, Arizona Western, Eastern Florida State, Phoenix College, Pima CC, Mohave CC, Glendale CC, Dodge City CC, Neosho County CC, Johnson County CC, Southeastern CC, Iowa Lakes CC, Blinn College, Coastal Bend College, Angelina College, LSU Eunice, Nassau CC, Ulster County CC, Suffolk CC, Westchester CC, Murray State (OK), Lewis & Clark CC, Otero College, Montgomery College, Yavapai College, Eastern Arizona College, College of Southern Nevada, Community Christian College, Eastern Oklahoma State, Connors State, Northeastern Oklahoma A&M, Rose State, National Park College, University of Arkansas Rich Mountain, Hill College, Western Texas College, Truman College, Daley College, Malcolm X College, Kennedy-King College, Wilbur Wright College, Coffeyville CC, Garden City CC, Seward County CC, Casper College, Northwest College, Central Wyoming College, Laramie County CC, Gillette College, Western Nebraska CC, Lamar CC, Trinidad State, Northeastern Junior College, USC Lancaster, USC Salkehatchie, USC Sumter, USC Union, Paris JC, Jacksonville College, Northeast Texas CC, Texas Southmost, Crowder College, Jefferson College (MO), Harcum College, Hagerstown CC, Harford CC, Salt Lake CC, Snow College, North Idaho College, College of Southern Idaho, Colorado Northwestern CC, Utah State Eastern, Truckee Meadows CC, Pacific Northwest Christian College, Illinois Central, Southwestern Illinois, Lincoln Trail, Central Georgia Tech, Ranger College, NOC Enid
scholarships: Athletic grants + need
relevance: 89 guide JUCO schools spanning 17 NJCAA regions the guide covers (Region 1 AZ/NV/CA, Region 2 OK/AR, Region 4 IL, Region 5 TX, Region 6 KS, Region 8 FL, Region 9 CO/WY/NE, Region 10 SC, Region 11 IA/NE, Region 14 TX/LA, Region 15 NY, Region 16 MO, Region 19 PA/DE/NJ, Region 20 MD, Region 24 IL, Region 18 UT/ID/CO/NV/WA) plus Santa Monica (CCCAA, non-NJCAA) — all 2-year transfer platforms. Region 16 (Missouri) and Region 19 (Pennsylvania) debut, and Region 20 grows to three schools: Crowder College won the 2025 Region 16 Tournament and reached the Plains District Tournament in first-year head coach Hunter Gilliam's debut season (Silas Laytham, NJCAA D1 3rd Team All-American); Jefferson College, led by program alumnus Luke Schlichting, reached the same final and carries a real UCM Kinesiology, BS articulation. Harcum College is this entire campaign's most decorated on-field program — a 2020-21 NJCAA DI National Championship Tournament Final Four (beating already-guide Western Texas College at Nationals) plus 2020 and 2024 East District titles, under head coach David Hughes, backed by a genuine clinical PTA A.S. degree — offset by the highest cost of attendance in the guide. Hagerstown CC (a measured 3-season coaching turnaround under Joe Mills) and Harford CC (the program's first Region 20 title in 50 years, 2024, plus a first-ever 2021 National Tournament berth, under head coach Bill Wardle's internationally-diverse roster) join Montgomery College in Region 20; neither offers on-campus housing. Region 10 (South Carolina) debuts with all four of the region's DI programs: USC Lancaster (2025 Region 10 DI Tournament Champion and NJCAA Southeast District Runner-up), USC Sumter (2024-25 Region 10 regular-season champion, 10-1-2, under a first-year head coach with a rare NCAA D1/D2/D3 CV), USC Union (program-best 2025-26 season and four consecutive Region 10 DI Players of the Year, 2022-2025), and USC Salkehatchie (a wide-open midfield under 16-year head coach William Glass, offsetting on-field decline). A fifth SC school, Denmark Technical College, was excluded after being found to have moved its soccer program to the USCAA for 2025-26. Region 9 grows to ten guide schools alongside Otero College with the addition of five Wyoming programs: Laramie County CC (11X Region IX Champions per the team's own account, a brand-new $31M athletics complex, and the campaign's strongest ACU-aligned Kinesiology degree), Casper College (a sustained NCAA D1/D2/NAIA transfer pipeline under program-founder head coach Ben McArthur), Northwest College (led by UEFA 'B'-licensed Rob Hill, returning the program to a 2025 Region 9 final), Gillette College (a purpose-built 2020 soccer field and a new $18.5M academic-athletic complex), and Central Wyoming College (a program in an early rebuilding phase under a first-season head coach). Region 6 (Kansas) grows to five guide schools with the addition of Coffeyville CC (NJCAA Academic Team of the Year 2025-26 for men's soccer, a dedicated Athletic Training AS degree), Garden City CC ('historic' 2025 season under alumnus head coach Oscar Zelaya, a 2008 NJCAA DI National Tournament 4th-place team player), and Seward County CC (the guide's youngest Kansas program, launched fall 2023, under founding head coach Jaime Beltran, a 2013 NJCAA DI Region 5 Champion as head coach at Ranger College). Region 4 (Chicago) debuts with all five City Colleges of Chicago programs: Harry S. Truman College (NJCAA Region 4 DI three-peat champion, 2023-2025, under a three-time Region 4 Coach of the Year), Richard J. Daley College (a genuine 3-year coaching turnaround, 1-11-3 to 8-6), Malcolm X College (the only campus with real on-campus exercise-science coursework, at CCC's $251M Health Sciences center), Kennedy-King College, and Wilbur Wright College (a newly NJCAA Foundation-grant-funded, still-developing program). Phoenix College are the 2025 NJCAA DII National Champions (ranked #1 nationally for 7 straight weeks). Indian Hills are 2025 NJCAA DI National Champions. Suffolk County CC won the 2025 NJCAA Region 15 Division III Championship — Region 15's only Division I program is Monroe University (New Rochelle); Suffolk, Nassau, Ulster County and Westchester all compete at Division III (corrected 2026-08-11, no athletic scholarships under NJCAA rules). Johnson County CC won the 2025 Region 6/9 title. Daytona State are 2025 NJCAA DI finalists — top-5 D1 transfer feeder. Tyler JC is the #1 D1 transfer feeder all-time. SMC → UCLA proven pipeline. Monroe are 3× NJCAA DI champions, NYC metro. Arizona Western pairs a #2 national ranking (2025) with a genuine Exercise/Wellness/Nutrition degree. Eastern Florida State plays in a 1,000-seat dedicated stadium. Murray State (OK) are back-to-back NJCAA DI National Tournament qualifiers (2024, 2025) and the guide's most freshman-open intake. Otero College and Montgomery College both won their 2025 Region/District titles and a National Tournament match. Yavapai College is a seven-time national champion program and 2025 Region 1 runner-up. College of Southern Nevada is the guide's only Region 1 JUCO in a genuine major city (Las Vegas). Region 2 (Oklahoma/Arkansas) now has seven guide schools: Murray State plus Eastern Oklahoma State, Rose State, Northeastern Oklahoma A&M, Connors State, and the newly-added National Park College (guide's newest program, founded 2024, best 2025-26 raw win total of its batch) and University of Arkansas Rich Mountain (outright Region 2 champion in 2019 and 2021, now led by a five-time NCAA D1 head coach). Region 5 (Texas) debuts with Hill College (2025 worst-to-first turnaround, Region 5 regular-season champion and Tournament runner-up, lowest cost in the guide's newest batch) and Western Texas College (2025 Region 5 Tournament Champion and NJCAA Mid-South District runner-up, the guide's only confirmed dedicated JUCO soccer complex among this group). Region 9 grows further with four Colorado/Nebraska programs: Western Nebraska CC (2024 Region IX champion, first-ever NJCAA DI National Tournament appearance, first-ever program All-American, cheapest COA in the batch at $14,125/yr), Trinidad State (alumnus HC Tyler Wilt returned 2025 after 4 years as HC at York University NE, the guide's only named direct AA-to-BS Exercise Science agreement with CSU Pueblo), Northeastern Junior College (fully-cleared 2025-26 midfield group, strongest-branded Athletic Training pathway of the batch), and Lamar CC (genuine Athletic Training Practicum clinical sequence, weakest recent on-field record of the batch under new HC Alieu Kamara). Region 14 (Texas) makes its guide debut with four schools that share one conference bracket in East/South Texas: Paris Junior College, Jacksonville College, Northeast Texas Community College, and Texas Southmost College. None carries a Region 14 title or postseason result in this campaign's 2021-2025 research window, and all four are genuinely modest on-field programs, but each has a real distinguishing story. Paris JC's transfer pipeline is growing fast under head coach Fernando Arellano (a former NCAA D1 player, NJCAA All-American, and Liga MX professional): a program-record 10 players signed to continue their careers in June 2026, up from 7 the year before, including back-to-back NCAA Division I transfers (Houston Christian 2025, Missouri State 2026). Northeast Texas CC's head coach Jon Evan carries one of the deepest individually-documented CVs in this entire campaign — assistant roles at two different NCAA Division I programs (including directly developing a future MLS SuperDraft pick), an NCAA D2 head-coaching conference title, and two separate NCAA D3 head-coaching program-best tenures — even though the program itself, in an early rebuild since his April 2023 hire, currently carries Region 14's weakest on-field record. Jacksonville College is the smallest school in this entire campaign (~550 students, a private Christian junior college) with a genuinely large, wide-open midfield pool heading into 2026-27. Texas Southmost College is the campaign's newest confirmed program — launched NJCAA competition in 2023-24 under founding head coach and TSC/UTB alumnus Mario Zamora, who holds a genuine binational Mexican FA (FMF) and US Soccer coaching license — and is the only school in this batch on a real city campus (Brownsville, on the US-Mexico border), though it has no on-campus housing anywhere in the TSC system, unlike Paris JC, Jacksonville, and Northeast Texas CC, which all offer real on-campus dorms. Region 18 (Utah/Idaho/Colorado/Nevada/Washington, Scenic West Athletic Conference) makes its guide debut with all eight schools sharing one conference bracket: Salt Lake CC, Snow College, North Idaho College, College of Southern Idaho, Colorado Northwestern CC, Utah State Eastern, Truckee Meadows CC, and Pacific Northwest Christian College. Salt Lake CC is the strongest on-field program found anywhere in this entire campaign — an undefeated 2021 NJCAA Division I National Championship (17-0) followed by four consecutive conference titles (2022-2024) and a 2025 Region 18 Tournament title, under head coach Mark Davis, in a genuine major-city Utah campus. Snow College won the program's first-ever conference title in 2025 and produced an NJCAA All-American (Isaac Stanley), now under brand-new head coach Lewis Wilson (an 8-year Aberdeen FC Academy product). Utah State Eastern's head coach Bruce Palmbaum holds a USSF 'A' Coaching License and NCAA Division I head-coaching experience (University of Tulsa) — one of the deepest individual coaching CVs in the entire campaign — and USU Eastern offers a genuine on-site Bachelor's degree (Health Science, BS) with real Kinesiology coursework. North Idaho College and Truckee Meadows CC each play at a real dedicated soccer facility (Eisenwinter Field and TMCC Soccer Field respectively); Truckee Meadows is also the guide's other genuine mid-size-city Region 18 campus (Reno, NV). College of Southern Idaho and Colorado Northwestern CC are both still-developing programs — CSI improving in only its second season under founding head coach Alex Ferreira, and Colorado Northwestern in a genuine multi-season rebuild now under new head coach Dave Brown, who arrives from an NJCAA regional-championship coaching staff. Pacific Northwest Christian College is the youngest and least-established program in this entire campaign (1-39 across its first three seasons), now under a brand-new first-time head coach, at one of the lowest costs of attendance in the guide. Region 24 (Illinois) grows to four guide schools alongside Lewis & Clark CC: Illinois Central College (a real 2022 Region 24 title and a No. 12 2024 national ranking under head coach Gabe Carreno), Southwestern Illinois College (head coach Lindsay Eversmeyer, the first and only woman ever to play men's professional soccer, a 4x regional Sports Hall of Fame inductee), and Lincoln Trail College (a program mid-rebuild under new head coach Luis Dantas, an NCAA D1 transfer and 3-season professional indoor soccer veteran). Central Georgia Technical College (Region 17, GA — the guide's Georgia debut) launched in 2023 and pairs steady improvement with a CAPTE-accredited PTA degree. Ranger College (Region 5, TX) has posted three straight above-.500 seasons and carries a 2013 Region 5 Championship in program history. Northern Oklahoma College-Enid (Region 2, OK) is home to the $12 million Advance Soccer Complex under one of the campaign's most experienced head coaches, though the program is mid-rebuild. A fourth planned school, Cisco College (TX), was excluded after being found to field women's soccer only.

name: NEC
mlsPipeline: Developing — NEC programs feed regional USL/NPSL pipelines
scholarships: NCAA D1 — up to 9.9 equivalencies; 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
relevance: Mercyhurst University (Erie, PA) — joined the NEC in Fall 2024 and won the NEC regular-season title in that first D1 season; 8th in 2025. Provisional D1 member — no NCAA postseason until 2028–29. HC Austin Solomon, building on a strong D2 PSAC base (back-to-back West titles 2021–22). Exercise Science B.S. with 500hr clinical. 2 Australians previously on roster.

name: CACC
scholarships: NCAA D2 — up to 9.0 equivalencies
relevance: Georgian Court University (Lakewood, NJ) — Dino Raso (13 seasons, 2024 CACC Coach of Year). B.S. Exercise Science Wellness & Sports with explicit Pre-PT/OT/PA tracks. Jersey Shore 20 min, NYC 90 min.

name: AMC
mlsPipeline: NAIA level — USL League Two pathway
scholarships: NAIA — 12 equivalencies, no per-player cap
relevance: ⚠ Columbia College MO — NO Exercise Science degree (Healthcare Management only). New HC Nathan Mason rebuilding. Best value cost (7k/yr) in guide. Mizzou college-town atmosphere. DPT pathway requires extra planning.

name: Summit
mlsPipeline: Developing — Denver drove the league's pipeline before leaving for the WCC in 2026
scholarships: NCAA D1 — up to 9.9 equivalencies (men's soccer); 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
relevance: Delaware (Newark, DE) — its men's soccer joined the Summit League in 2025 after the school's all-sports move to Conference USA, which does not sponsor the sport; reached the 2025 Summit League semifinals (12-2-3, #24 nationally). Only Summit school in the guide, filed here rather than under the CAA. Strong Kinesiology & Applied Physiology degree; low ~$38k cost; Philadelphia Union (MLS) 25 min north.

name: Patriot League
mlsPipeline: Developing — service-academy programs; limited pro pathway
scholarships: Full federal scholarships (service academies) — no athletic-aid cap
relevance: Army West Point and Navy compete in the Patriot League for men's soccer — their AAC membership is for other sports. Both are service academies (full federal scholarship, zero cost) but carry a military service commitment incompatible with Olivier's DPT/MLS path — a narrative warning, not a soccer knock. Army won the 2022 Patriot League regular season; Navy plays a full Patriot schedule from a strong east-coast base.
